prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: checked baggage from acceptance at bag-drop or transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up and handoff for aircraft loading. The boundary includes the airport conveyance, screening, routing, reconciliation and staging equipment and controls. It excludes airline aircraft loading beyond the handoff at the outbound load control point.

Induction: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (passenger interface; captures bag identification and accepts bags). Transfer Bag Feeder (separate induction for eligible transfer bags). Induction Tray Conveyor (presents bags in a controlled manner to screening and sorting).

Control: Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (coordinates bag status, routing decisions and operational visibility; uses current flight and operating data to align routing with departures). Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (coordinates local equipment and conveyance in its area; produces the Recovery Route Card). Flight Data Gateway (sends the Flight Cutoff Advisory; receiver not yet stated).

Screening: North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner (screening interfaces). Image Resolution Desk (operator review of screening images when automated processing needs assessment). Secondary Inspection Chute (path for bags selected for additional examination). Explosives Response Team and Security Duty Manager (actors; coordinate security response and disposition of escalated screening events).

Sorting and reconciliation: Primary Crossbelt Sorter (routes cleared bags to make-up areas). Bag Reconciliation Station (verifies bag identity and processing status when records or physical handling need reconciliation).

Make-up and handoff: East Make-Up Conveyor and West Make-Up Conveyor (convey routed bags toward loading areas). Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (stages bags for its assigned departure). Outbound Load Control Desk (confirms baggage readiness at the aircraft-loading handoff). Airline Ramp Coordinator (actor; coordinates acceptance of staged bags for ramp operations).

No modes or normative requirements have been stated so far.

Document units:
S024: The Baggage Operations Supervisor oversees routine flow, responds to service interruptions, and coordinates operational recovery with the Security Duty Manager and Maintenance Technician.
S025: Service objectives are to maintain safe screening, accurate bag-to-flight association, predictable throughput, and timely delivery within applicable departure cutoffs.
S026: Equipment status, bag identity, routing state, and operating restrictions are exchanged through defined interfaces, with local staff responsible for resolving conditions that automated controls cannot clear.
S027: Check-in acceptance begins when staff confirm that the bag is eligible for carriage under the applicable airline rules.
S028: Staff verify the passenger and flight details before accepting the bag into the checked-baggage process.
S029: The Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit records the accepted bag and initiates its processing.
S030: The Bag Tag Printer produces a durable tag with a unique identifier for each accepted bag.
S031: The tag identifier is associated with the passenger and flight record in the Baggage Control System.
S032: The Baggage Control System checks that the flight is open for bag acceptance and that the bag record is complete.
S033: Bags with missing, unreadable, or conflicting acceptance data are held for staff resolution before induction.
S034: Staff check bag dimensions and weight against the configured limits for standard conveyor handling.
S035: The Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit sends an Oversize Exception Ticket when a checked bag exceeds the configured size envelope.
S036: Oversized bags remain in a designated holding area until staff confirm an approved handling route.
S037: The Transfer Bag Feeder identifies each inbound transfer bag and records its arrival into the local handling process.
S038: The Transfer Bag Feeder sends a Late Transfer Bag Card when a bag enters from an inbound transfer stream.
S039: Staff confirm that transfer-bag identifiers are legible and correspond to a valid onward flight record.
S040: The Baggage Control System compares transfer-bag data with the current routing information before the bag is released for induction.
S041: The Flight Data Gateway supplies flight and routing records used for acceptance and induction decisions.
S042: Before induction, the bag record must be valid, the selected route must be available, and the receiving equipment must be ready.
S043: The Concourse Zone Controller grants an induction permissive only when local equipment status and operating restrictions allow movement.
S044: The Induction Tray Conveyor accepts bags through controlled feed points and maintains separation between successive bags.
